extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners operating under Singapore law (IPOS users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for examination of patent applications before the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS), covering claim construction, novelty, inventive step, application formalities, unity, amendments, patentable subject matter, supplementary examination, examination review and re-examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters to be determined during examination (Rule 2A(1) / Section 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting examination the Examiner must determine, inter alia, whether, taking into account all relevant prior art, each claim satisfies each condition or requirement for patentability under section 13; whether the conditions in section 25(4) and (5) have been complied with; whether the application discloses any additional matter referred to in section 84(1) or (2) or any matter in section 84(3); and whether there is any other application or earlier grant for the same invention with the same priority date to the same applicant or successor in title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must consider all relevant prior art discovered by search or otherwise. This is the primary statutory checklist framing examination work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should assess patentability matters on the balance of probabilities but consider whether there is a substantial doubt on a fact that gives a reasonable prospect that the matter may turn out differently at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a balance of probabilities; where substantial doubt exists and a reasonable prospect that full trial/expert evidence could alter the outcome, allow the application to proceed rather than refuse. Consider applicant's opportunity to present material — less scope for doubt when applicant had full opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposive construction of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be interpreted purposively: what would the person skilled in the art have understood the patentee to mean by the language of the claims, read in light of the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is objective and not concerned with the patentee's subjective intentions. Use purposive approach consistently for examination (validity, novelty, infringement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be construed consistently regardless of subject matter; avoid construing broadly for novelty and narrowly for support (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret claims in the same way for both infringement and validity considerations to provide certainty to public and patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical techniques for claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips: read the claims before the description; draw the invention from the definition given in the claims; consult with other Examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques help avoid importing 'gloss' from description/drawings into the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 113(1) scope principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of protection conferred is that specified in a claim as interpreted by the description and drawings (Section 113(1)): codifies purposive approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are interpreted in light of the whole specification and drawings; not purely literal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of variants and unessential features
rubrics_metrics.description: A purposive construction may treat variants that have no material effect on how the invention works as within the claim; exclude variants that would have a material effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether a variant would have a material effect from the viewpoint of the skilled person. Examples: small angular deviations that have negligible functional effect may fall within claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: No doctrine of equivalents beyond the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection cannot extend beyond the claims — purposive construction does not create a separate doctrine of equivalents that expands claim scope beyond claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal limits set by Kirin-Amgen and subsequent cases: ensure claim scope remains within claim language as purposively construed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Improver/Protocol questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Improver (Protocol) questions to determine whether a variant falls within the claim (guidance for equivalents analysis under purposive construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these established questions when assessing whether a variant is covered by the claim under purposive construction (case law guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person skilled in the art — role and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are construed from the viewpoint of the person skilled in the art; that person's common general knowledge informs interpretation and enablement assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making findings about what the skilled person knows without evidence; where common general knowledge is unclear, expert evidence may materially affect outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding importing gloss or re-drafting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should avoid reading limitations from the description/drawings into the claims that are not expressed by the language of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction should not become claim re-drafting; preserve claim boundaries as written unless clearly supported by the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special meanings and claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification assigns a special meaning to a term, that special meaning governs construction; otherwise ordinary meaning in context applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and apply special definitions from the description; otherwise interpret terms as the skilled person would.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and dependent claims interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims define the invention; dependent claims incorporate features of claims they depend on and may limit scope accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider dependencies in assessing novelty, inventive step, support and sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open- and closed-ended terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and treat open-ended (e.g., 'comprising') and closed-ended (e.g., 'consisting of') claim language appropriately in scope assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended language generally allows additional unspecified features; closed-ended limits to stated features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of reference numbers in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference numbers in drawings are generally not limiting unless the claim language makes them so or the specification indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not import unnecessary limitations from reference numerals into claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-for / Method-for / Use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance applies to 'product for …', 'method for …', and 'use of … in …' claim formats regarding what is claimed and how to assess novelty/inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess such claim forms with attention to their functional language and possible requirement to link to a new technical effect or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Product-by-process claims are claims to products defined by the process by which they are made; novelty/infringement assessed by product identity, not merely process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether product is distinguishable by structure/composition or just by process; careful when process imparts distinguishing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives / Markush claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush or alternative claim groupings must be clear and properly structured so that each alternative is supported and enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure alternatives are not so numerous or unrelated as to cause unity/support/clarity problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — each and every feature disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A document anticipates (destroys novelty of) a claim only if it discloses each and every feature of the claim (explicitly or implicitly/inherently), with enablement where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess explicit disclosure, implicit disclosure and inheritability; distinguish between novelty and inventive step issues if differences exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit and inherent disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior disclosure can anticipate if it implicitly or inherently discloses missing features — i.e., the skilled person would inevitably have derived the feature from the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful factual analysis needed to decide whether a feature is inherent; mere possibility is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and enabling disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For a prior publication to be novelty-destroying, it must have been made available to the public and must enable the relevant subject matter to the skilled person (as required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish date of availability and whether the disclosure is enabling for the claimed subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of ranges and parametric claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations apply where prior art discloses ranges or parameters; whether a claimed sub-range or parameter is anticipated depends on disclosure and whether the skilled person would derive the claimed range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess disclosure of end-points, preferred ranges, and whether claimed values are specially singled out or arbitrary selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior public uses can be novelty-destroying if their date of public availability can be established and the skilled person could work the invention from the prior use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require evidence that the use was sufficiently public and enabling; corroboration often needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to novelty — grace period and learned society disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: There are statutory exceptions such as grace periods; details and limits of exceptions must be applied according to the Patents Act provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine timing and circumstances carefully to determine whether a disclosure falls within an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step — statutory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claimed invention involves an inventive step (non-obviousness) over relevant prior art under Section 13 and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established tests/case law to avoid hindsight and assess inventive concept, starting point, and whether the invention would have been obvious to try.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for inventive step — Windsurfing / Pozzoli (modified Windsurfing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Windsurfing test and the modified 'Pozzoli' approach to identify the inventive concept, establish the closest prior art, and decide obviousness by reference to the skilled person's common general knowledge and whether combination or modification would be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-step approach: identify inventive concept, differences from prior art, objective technical problem and whether differences would have been obvious to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding hindsight in inventive step assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using the claimed invention as a template; analysis must be from the skilled person's perspective at the priority/filing date without knowledge of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use careful stepwise analysis, credible evidence, and avoid combining teachings in an impermissible 'mosaicing' unless the skilled person would have been led to combine them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining disclosures (mosaicing) for inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining multiple prior art disclosures to arrive at the claimed invention is permissible only if the skilled person would have been motivated to combine them with a reasonable expectation of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider motivation to combine, reasonable expectation, and whether combination requires impermissible hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious to try and selection inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider 'obvious to try' tests (was it obvious to try a route with a reasonable expectation of success) and special rules for selection inventions where a subset is claimed from a broader class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether routine trials would have been undertaken by the skilled person and whether success would have been reasonably expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary indicia in inventive step (commercial success, long‑felt want, technical prejudice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary considerations such as commercial success, long-felt but unsolved needs, overcoming technical prejudice, and unexpected advantages may be relevant to inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat secondary indicia as supporting evidence; weigh them with primary inventive-step analysis rather than as determinative alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory application formalities and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must comply with statutory requirements (e.g., claims numbering, number of claims per Rule 19(6), claims drafted in technical terms per Rule 19(7), two-part form per Rule 19(8), omnibus claims Rule 19(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check formal compliance: numbering, claim count, claim form and technical wording per the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Section 25(4) and 25(5)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must disclose the invention sufficiently for the skilled person to perform it; description must enable the invention across the breadth of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess enabling disclosure, role of skilled person, clarity of description, and whether undue burden is required to practice the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims define the matter for which protection is sought (Section 25(5)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define the subject-matter for which protection is sought; they must be clear and adequately set out the boundaries of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims correspond to the technical contribution and are not mere statements of intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness of claims (Section 25(5)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear and concise; avoid indefinite terms, unexplained relative terms, lack of antecedent, inconsistent language, overly broad multiple alternatives and unnecessarily verbose claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess each of the enumerated clarity issues (indefinite terms, relative terms, preferred/optional definitions, ranges, single-ingredient compositions, multiple alternatives, inconsistencies between claims and description, conciseness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to be supported by the description (Section 25(5)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by the description — mere coincidence of language is insufficient; claims must reflect the technical contribution and be enabled by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate support in terms of essential features, features defined by function, parametric claims, reach-through claims and whether the description provides clear basis for the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and enabling requirements for the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must provide enabling disclosure, the role of the skilled person must be clear, the description must be comprehensible, and references to prior art, trademarks and standards should be used carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the specification allows the skilled person to carry out the invention across its claimed scope without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and sequence listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract and sequence listings must comply with statutory/formal requirements to enable appropriate publication and searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check format and content requirements, and inclusion of required sequence listings where biological sequences are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Section 26 and related rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must meet unity of invention requirements: claims should relate to a single inventive concept or be linked such that a single general inventive concept is present; lack of unity can be a priori or a posteriori.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess unity objectively; avoid literal or over-technical approaches; flag unduly complex claims, mixed categories, Markush/group claims issues; follow approach for determining lack of unity in Singapore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination where multiple inventions present
rubrics_metrics.description: If lack of unity is found, Examiner must consider search scope, invite divisional filing or additional fees, and apply rules for examining additional inventions and handling divisionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory and procedural rules for search/examining multiple inventions and for divisional applications and double patenting considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General power to amend before and after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: There is statutory power to amend applications before grant and patents after grant subject to Rules (e.g., Rule 46, Section 38) and allowability criteria in Section 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural steps for amendments (process and timelines); ensure amendments do not add matter or extend protection beyond original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of pre-grant and post-grant amendments (Section 84(3) & 84(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must not introduce additional matter (not supported by the application as filed) and must not extend the protection conferred by the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply baseline criteria (clear & concise; supported by description) and consider discretionary factors such as delay, unfair advantage, and conduct of patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for added subject matter / added matter (two-part and related tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Added matter assessment uses tests requiring that amendments be clearly and unambiguously disclosed in the application as filed (no new technical information beyond original disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare amendment to original filing disclosure; consider express and implicit disclosures, intermediate generalisation, generic-to-specific conversions, ranges and disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections under Section 107 — two‑step test
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to a patent must satisfy the statutory two-step test for correction (e.g., obvious clerical errors, error evident on the document etc.) per Section 107 and jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the two-step test strictly; treat translation errors and other alleged errors with care and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exclusions: non-patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, aesthetic creations, schemes/rules/methods for mental acts, games or business, and presentation of information are excluded from patentable subject matter unless they provide a technical contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess industrial applicability and technical contribution; apply exclusion categories carefully with reference to case law and examples in Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention must be susceptible of industrial application — capable of being made or used in any kind of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject claims contrary to established physical laws and those incapable of practical application (e.g., perpetual motion machines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of medical treatment and medical use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules govern patentability of methods of medical treatment, surgery, diagnosis and first/second medical use claims, with detailed examples and limits set out in Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether claimed medical methods are excluded or allowable depending on formulation of claims (e.g., second medical use 'Swiss-type' or purpose‑limited product claims) and statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnological subject matter (devices, antibodies, microorganisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance applies to biotech inventions, including deposit of micro-organisms, claims to antibodies and device claims; special support, enablement and patentable subject matter considerations apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check compliance with deposit requirements, sufficiency for biological materials, and particular case law on antibodies and biotech claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morality and ethical exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter contrary to morality (e.g., certain human cloning, generation of human embryos) may be excluded from patentability under statutory/moral grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply morality exclusions conservatively and in line with statutory text and case law examples in Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary examination (requirements and process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary examination for certain national/regional/PCT situations requires prescribed documents (e.g., corresponding applications, certified copies, translations) and follows defined process and grounds (including claim relatedness and medical use claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required documents are provided within prescribed time limits and that supporting documents are verified and correctly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party observations and raising new prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may submit observations and prior art during examination; Examiner should consider such submissions and may raise objections based on them where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify dates, translations and relevance of third-party documents; consider whether documents present new arguments or merely rehash prior submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a formal examination review process for unresolved objections with prescribed steps for requesting review, preparation of examination review reports and consideration of unresolved objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural steps and timelines; ensure timely responses and proper recording of review findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte re-examination — acceptance requirements (Section 38A(2), Rule 52A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-examination request must be filed in the prescribed manner, accompanied by the prescribed fee, reasons to substantiate the grounds and any documents considered relevant at the time of filing; translations and verifications required for non-English documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request may be rejected if procedural requirements not met; supporting documents should be filed with the request and dates of public availability established where relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and form of re-examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must clearly identify each ground for re-examination, explain how each ground is established, identify claims affected, and where prior art is relied upon, point to relevant portions and map claim features to prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructions and new arguments if relying on previously considered documents; file supporting documents/English translations and verifications together with the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar discretion to reject frivolous or abusive re-examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar must not grant re-examination requests that are frivolous, vexatious, or abuse of process (e.g., repeated submissions of same grounds or equivalent documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether request repeats rejected grounds or relies on family members/equivalent documents such that it's abusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with court proceedings for re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar will not accept a re-examination request where court or Registrar proceedings are pending that may put validity in issue; Registrar has discretion if such proceedings are filed after a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check procedural status before accepting re-examination; exercise Registrar's discretion where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Examiner's consideration in re-examination (Section 38A(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: During re-examination, Examiner determines whether grounds specified are made out and may report on any other grounds in Section 38A(1) based on submitted documents; Examiner may examine claims not identified in the request if relevant documents support doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners primarily rely on documents submitted by requester but may cite additional documents to establish common general knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion and re-examination report procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If Examiner finds grounds are made out, a written opinion is provided to the proprietor; proprietor has one opportunity (three months) to respond with submissions and/or amendments; Examiner draws up the re-examination report considering responses and any oppositions to proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 52A timelines: proprietor's single response window, publication/advertisement of proposed amendments, opposition period, and the requirement that amendments satisfy Section 84(4) and baseline criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability criteria for proposed amendments during re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments must not add matter or extend protection (Section 84(4)); discretionary factors such as sufficient disclosure, unreasonable delay, unfair advantage, and conduct of patentee affect allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess amendments against both substantive (no added matter/no extension) and discretionary conduct-based factors; proposed amendments may be opposed and reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview requests during re-examination (Rule 52A(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietor may request one interview within prescribed time limit after receiving written opinion; interview should be accompanied by an agenda and any proposed amendments should be tabled and provided with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews typically limited to agenda items, normally up to two hours, and Registrar obliged to grant only one interview in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of re-examination (maintenance, amendment or revocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: After re-examination report issuance, the patent will be maintained as original, maintained in amended form, or revoked (conditional or unconditional); proprietor may have final opportunity to amend to avoid revocation and may appeal to Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unresolved objections remain, Registrar must order revocation (conditional or unconditional); proprietor may amend under Section 83 within time limit to avoid full revocation and may appeal under Section 90.
